\caption{Value accuracy is not control accuracy. The control is the deliverable of an HJB and is a derivative of the value function, so the two errors need not track each other. Both errors are relative $L^2$ norms ($\|a-a^{\star}\|_2/\|a^{\star}\|_2$) and every order in this table is the least-squares slope of $\log$(error) against $\log h$. \emph{Top}: both errors against the closed-form reference, with the observed order of the control error. \emph{Middle}: with the mesh fixed and only the number of stored snapshots changed, the value error falls by up to two orders of magnitude while the control error improves by at most a factor of about $23$ and then plateaus -- the two are limited by different refinements. \emph{Bottom}: for each sweep, the least-squares control order with its fit quality, and the control/value error ratio from its first to its largest value. The order is the robust statement; the ratio is a ratio of two convergences and turns over wherever the value error regresses, so it is summarised rather than printed in full. The fourth row shows what happens when the solver's snapshot memory cap silently coarsens the time resolution as $N^5$ grows -- the fit degenerates and the order is meaningless -- and the last row reruns $p=5$ with the cap raised so the time resolution is held fixed (Section~\ref{sec:control}).}
